name: Jean Louise Finch
hint1: She is on stage a lot but is rarely part of the action.
hint2: She speaks straight to the audience.
hint3: She watches her younger self.
hint4: She is the girl from the story, now a woman, telling it.

name: Jean Louise Finch
hint1: Her voice opens the play.
hint2: She looks back on her childhood in Maycomb.
hint3: At the end, she says she learned to stand in other people's shoes.
hint4: She is Scout, years later, telling the audience what happened.

name: Scout
description: Jean Louise as a young girl
hint1: She is ready to fight anyone who insults her father.
hint2: She kicks a man in the mob outside the jail.
hint3: She talks to Mr Cunningham about his son until the men go home.
hint4: She is the younger Finch child.

name: Scout
description: Jean Louise as a young girl
hint1: She sits up in the balcony during the trial.
hint2: She is attacked in the dark on the way home.
hint3: She stands on the Radley porch and sees the street as its owner does.
hint4: She is Atticus's daughter, the girl the narrator used to be.

name: Jem
hint1: He wants his father to play in a football game.
hint2: After the mad dog, he sees his father in a new light.
hint3: He goes to the jail with his sister and Dill to find his father.
hint4: He is the older of Atticus's two children.

name: Jem
hint1: He loves football.
hint2: He loses his temper when an old neighbour insults his father.
hint3: His punishment is to spend every afternoon for a month with her.
hint4: His elbow is broken when Bob Ewell attacks him.

name: Atticus Finch
description: Their father; Tom Robinson's defence lawyer
hint1: He says he is too old to play football.
hint2: He kills a mad dog with one shot.
hint3: He sits alone outside the jail at night.
hint4: He defends the accused man in court.

name: Atticus Finch
description: Their father; Tom Robinson's defence lawyer
hint1: Bob Ewell spits in his face.
hint2: He proves in court that Bob Ewell is left-handed.
hint3: His closing speech is made straight to the audience, as if they were the jury.
hint4: He is Scout and Jem's dad, a lawyer in Maycomb.

name: Calpurnia
hint1: She helps to bring up two children who have no mother.
hint2: She is strict with Scout about how to behave.
hint3: She works for the Finches every day.
hint4: She runs the Finch home and keeps the children in line.

name: Calpurnia
hint1: The children have to do what she says while their father is at work.
hint2: She cooks the family's meals.
hint3: She is the Black woman who helps to bring up two white children.
hint4: She is the Finches' housekeeper.

name: Maudie Atkinson
hint1: She laughs at the scary stories people tell about Boo.
hint2: She explains why it is a sin to kill a mockingbird.
hint3: She tells Jem that Maycomb trusts Atticus to do what is right.
hint4: She is the friendly woman on the Finches' street who takes the children's side.

name: Maudie Atkinson
hint1: She is a grown-up the children can always talk to.
hint2: She is on the Finches' side when much of the town is against them.
hint3: She explains to Jem why the case was given to his father.
hint4: She is the neighbour who never spreads rumours.

name: Stephanie Crawford
hint1: She says the mad dog might not have been mad at all.
hint2: She admits she felt safer when Atticus picked up the rifle.
hint3: She always seems to know everybody's business.
hint4: She loves spreading news about everyone on the street.

name: Stephanie Crawford
hint1: She enjoys a scandal.
hint2: She tells the children frightening tales about the house down the street.
hint3: If something happens in Maycomb, she has heard about it first.
hint4: She is the town gossip.

name: Mrs Dubose
description: The elderly neighbour whose flowers Jem destroys
hint1: Atticus says she was braver than anyone he knew.
hint2: She was fighting an addiction to morphine.
hint3: She shouts insults about Atticus at the children.
hint4: Her garden is wrecked by a furious boy.

name: Mrs Dubose
description: The elderly neighbour whose flowers Jem destroys
hint1: She lives two doors down from the Finches.
hint2: She makes rude remarks to the children whenever they pass.
hint3: Jem has to spend his afternoons with her as a punishment.
hint4: Jem cuts the heads off her camellias.

name: Nathan Radley
hint1: He is the only one in his house the children ever see.
hint2: He walks to town and back without stopping to chat.
hint3: He keeps the family house closed up and quiet.
hint4: He shares a home with the neighbour who never comes out.

name: Nathan Radley
hint1: He says an oak in his yard is sick.
hint2: He fills a hollow in that oak.
hint3: After he does it, no more presents appear.
hint4: He is Boo's older brother, who blocks up the knot-hole.

name: Boo Radley
hint1: Dill wants to make him come out.
hint2: Stories say he is a monster, but he is gentle.
hint3: He leaves gum in a knot-hole for the children.
hint4: He saves Jem and Scout from Bob Ewell.

name: Boo Radley
hint1: The children have never seen him.
hint2: He carries an injured boy home in the dark.
hint3: Heck Tate keeps his part in a death secret.
hint4: He is Scout's mysterious neighbour who never comes out.

name: Dill
hint1: He wants to make Boo Radley come out.
hint2: He runs away from home and turns up in Maycomb.
hint3: He cries in court at the way Tom is treated.
hint4: He is the boy who comes to stay every year when school is out.

name: Dill
hint1: He is small for his age but full of big ideas.
hint2: He goes to the jail with Jem and Scout.
hint3: He comes from Meridian.
hint4: He is Scout and Jem's friend who visits in the summer.

name: Heck Tate
hint1: He is the first witness at the trial.
hint2: He asks Atticus to deal with a mad animal in the street.
hint3: He warns Atticus that trouble is coming to the jail.
hint4: He is Maycomb County's top law officer.

name: Heck Tate
hint1: He brings Atticus the news that Tom is dead.
hint2: He says in court that Mayella had been beaten.
hint3: He decides what the official story of a death will be.
hint4: He is the sheriff who keeps a shy man out of the spotlight.

name: Judge Taylor
hint1: He tells the crowd to be quiet or leave.
hint2: Everyone stands when he comes in.
hint3: He listens to Atticus and Mr Gilmer argue.
hint4: He is in charge when Tom's case is heard.

name: Judge Taylor
hint1: He sits higher than everyone else in the room.
hint2: He bangs his gavel when the people watching get noisy.
hint3: He gave Atticus the case.
hint4: He is the man in the black robe at the trial.

name: Reverend Sykes
hint1: He makes room for three white children in the balcony.
hint2: He sits with Jem, Scout and Dill during the trial.
hint3: He tells Scout to stand up as her father walks past.
hint4: He leads the Black congregation in Maycomb.

name: Reverend Sykes
hint1: He is a respected man of God.
hint2: He looks after the children upstairs in the courthouse.
hint3: He is a leader of Tom's community.
hint4: He is the pastor of Tom's church.

name: Helen Robinson
hint1: Her family's life is turned upside down by one accusation.
hint2: She has to wait to hear what the jury decides.
hint3: The man she married is shot trying to escape.
hint4: She is married to the man Atticus defends.

name: Helen Robinson
hint1: She is one of the Black people of Maycomb who follow the trial closely.
hint2: She belongs to Reverend Sykes's church.
hint3: She loses her husband after the trial.
hint4: She is Tom's wife.

name: Mayella Ewell
hint1: Her story falls apart when Atticus questions her.
hint2: She says she called a man in to do a job for her.
hint3: She was beaten, and the evidence points to her own family.
hint4: She is the young woman whose claim puts a man on trial.

name: Mayella Ewell
hint1: She has no real friends.
hint2: Her father claims he saw the attack.
hint3: Atticus suggests the person who hurt her was left-handed.
hint4: She is Bob's girl, who says Tom attacked her.

name: Bob Ewell
hint1: He signs his name with his left hand.
hint2: He calls Tom's death good news.
hint3: He threatens Atticus after the trial.
hint4: He attacks Jem and Scout in the dark.

name: Bob Ewell
hint1: Atticus shows that he probably beat Mayella himself.
hint2: He spits in Atticus's face.
hint3: According to Heck Tate, he fell on his own blade.
hint4: He is Mayella's father, who accuses Tom.

name: Mr Gilmer
hint1: His questions make Dill cry.
hint2: He is rude and scornful to the man on the witness stand.
hint3: He calls Heck Tate, Bob and Mayella as witnesses.
hint4: He argues against Atticus in court.

name: Mr Gilmer
hint1: He works for the state, not for the man accused.
hint2: He mocks Tom for feeling sorry for a white woman.
hint3: Dill can't bear the way he speaks.
hint4: He is the prosecuting lawyer at Tom's trial.

name: Tom Robinson
hint1: His left hand was crippled in an accident.
hint2: He says he felt sorry for a white woman.
hint3: He is shot trying to escape from prison.
hint4: Atticus defends him in court.

name: Tom Robinson
hint1: A mob comes to the jail to get him.
hint2: He often helped Mayella with jobs for nothing.
hint3: The jury finds him guilty although he is innocent.
hint4: He is the man accused of attacking Mayella Ewell.

name: Mr Cunningham
hint1: He has a legal problem called an entailment.
hint2: His son is in Scout's class at school.
hint3: Scout's polite chat makes him feel ashamed outside the jail.
hint4: He tells the men at the jail to go home.

name: Mr Cunningham
hint1: Atticus has helped him with a legal problem.
hint2: He is one of the men who come at night to get Tom.
hint3: A little girl reminds him that he is a father too.
hint4: He is a poor farmer from outside Maycomb.
